classification.difficultyReason: The hardest figures require recognising two connected isosceles triangles or establishing an equilateral triangle before transferring angles through parallel lines and equating side expressions; the intermediate deductions are not supplied.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\theta$ and $x$. Different methods are combined in each part of this question.

spec.description: P, Q and R are collinear; their line is parallel to TS. QS and RS have matching double ticks.
spec.mathematics: Angle PTS is 70 degrees, PQS is 140 degrees; unknowns are TPQ, TSQ and QRS.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.short:
$\alpha=40^\circ$, $\beta=110^\circ$, $\gamma=40^\circ$.

Use parallel-line angles and the equal base angles of $\triangle QRS$.
answer.worked:
Co-interior angles, $PQ\parallel TS$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+140^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $PR\parallel TS$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+70^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line $PQR$ give $\angle SQR=180^\circ-140^\circ=40^\circ$. Since $QS=RS$, the base angles of $\triangle QRS$ are equal, so $\gamma=40^\circ$.

spec.description: Hourglass figure with AB parallel to CD; A, M, D and B, M, C are collinear.
spec.mathematics: BAM is 50 degrees and CMD is 70 degrees; find MCD.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and theta are visible.

answer.worked:
$\angle AMB=70^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).

Angle sum of $\triangle ABM$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABM+50^\circ+70^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle ABM&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
$\theta=60^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

spec.description: M lies on BA; BM, MA and MO have matching double ticks. No right-angle marker is present.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 35-degree angle and alpha are visible.

answer.worked:
$BM=MO$, so $\angle BOM=35^\circ$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle BMO$).

$\angle OMA=35^\circ+35^\circ=70^\circ$ (exterior angle of $\triangle BMO$).

$MA=MO$, so $\angle MOA=\alpha$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle MAO$).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\alpha+70^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=110^\circ\\\alpha&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: P and Q lie on OX and OY; PQ is parallel to XY. Theta is below PQ at Q.
spec.mathematics: XOY is 40 degrees and OXY is 65 degrees; theta is PQY.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied values and theta are visible.

answer.worked:
$\angle OPQ=65^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $PQ\parallel XY$).

Exterior angle of $\triangle OPQ$:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=40^\circ+65^\circ\\\theta&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: AF is parallel to BCG; AB and BC carry matching double ticks.
spec.mathematics: FAC is 40 degrees; theta is ABC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied angle and theta are visible.

answer.worked:
$\angle ACB=40^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AF\parallel BG$).

$AB=BC$, so $\angle BAC=40^\circ$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$).

Angle sum of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\theta+40^\circ+40^\circ&=180^\circ\\\theta&=100^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: ABC and ACD share AC; BC is perpendicular to AC, BA is parallel to CD, and AC equals AD.
spec.mathematics: ACD is 60 degrees; AD is 3x+5 and CD is 2x+4. Unknowns are CAD and ABC and x.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels are visible; no computed values are included.

answer.short:
$\alpha=60^\circ$, $\beta=30^\circ$, $x=-1$.

First establish that $\triangle ACD$ is equilateral.
answer.worked:
$AC=AD$, so $\angle ADC=\angle ACD=60^\circ$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ACD$).
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+60^\circ+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle ACD$ is equilateral.

$\angle BAC=60^\circ$ (alternate angles, $BA\parallel CD$).
$$\begin{align*}\beta+90^\circ+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $AD=CD$:
$$\begin{align*}3x+5&=2x+4\\x+5&=4\\x&=-1\end{align*}$$

spec.description: BA is parallel to DE. The unlabelled intersection of BC and DE is the vertex of a triangle whose sides to C and D have matching single ticks. The internal coordinate name I is not printed.
spec.mathematics: ABC is 65 degrees; alpha and beta are adjacent angles at the intersection and gamma is at D.
spec.answerVisibility: No intersection label or computed angle is printed.

answer.short:
$\alpha=65^\circ$, $\beta=115^\circ$, $\gamma=32\tfrac12^\circ$.

Use corresponding angles, supplementary angles and equal base angles.
answer.worked:
$\alpha=65^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel ED$).

Angles on a straight line:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+65^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$
The two marked equal sides form an isosceles triangle, so its angles at $C$ and $D$ are both $\gamma$.
$$\begin{align*}2\gamma+115^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\gamma&=65^\circ\\\gamma&=32\tfrac12^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with AD extended to E; single arrows mark BC and AD, double arrows mark AB and DC.
spec.mathematics: BAD is 60 degrees; unknowns are ABC, BCD and CDE.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles, $AD\parallel BC$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $AB\parallel CD$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+120^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
$\gamma=60^\circ$ (corresponding angles, $AB\parallel CD$).
